Definition: Naamah, the name of an antediluvian woman, of an Ammonitess, and of a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Naamah is the name of three different bearers in Scripture, and the best known is the Ammonitess who became the mother of a king. In 1 Kings 14:21 Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigns in Judah, and his mother is named as Naamah the Ammonitess, and 2 Chronicles 12:13 names her again at the same point in his story. The name also belongs to a daughter of Lamech in the earliest generations and to a town in Judah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Naamah is a reminder that God writes outsiders into the royal line. An Ammonite woman stands at the head of Judah's kings, and her son's story is told with her name attached, and God does not erase where a person came from when He gives them a place in His story.
